logical_component_title: JWT-based Authentication Token Lifecycle and Session Management

vulnerabilities.title: Null dereference risk in access-token flow (user lookup may be None)
vulnerabilities.description: In get_current_user_from_access_token, after decoding the token, the code fetches the user by email and then immediately accesses user.session_active. If no user is found (i.e., user is None), this causes an AttributeError when evaluating user.session_active, potentially leading to a 500 error and a denial of service or disclosure of stack traces in logs.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Fetch the user first, check for None, and only then evaluate session_active. Example: with Session(engine) as session: user = session.exec(select(User).where(User.email == token_data.sub)).first() if user is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Could not find user") if not user.session_active and not ignore_session_active: raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Session not active") Update last_active after confirming user exists.

vulnerabilities.title: Exception handling bug in refresh-token flow references undefined token_data
vulnerabilities.description: In get_current_user_from_refresh_token, the code decodes the token and builds token_data. If a JWTError or ValidationError occurs, the code enters the except block which then references token_data.sub to look up the user. If decoding failed, token_data may not be defined, causing a crash or invalid behavior. This can also lead to improper revocation decisions if the exception path depends on token_data.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Only reference token_data after successful decoding. Move the user lookup inside the try block after token_data is constructed, and in the except block return a 403/401 without accessing token_data. Alternatively set a safe fallback (e.g., do not access token_data in except).
vulnerabilities.snippet:
try:
    payload = jwt.decode(token, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
    token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    # proceed with token_data...
except(jwt.JWTError, ValidationError):
    # Do not reference token_data here; return error and revoke as needed
    raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Could not validate credentials", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})

vulnerabilities.title: Refresh flow lacks rotation; refresh tokens are not rotated and can be reused
vulnerabilities.description: The refresh endpoint validates the refresh token but returns only a new access token. There is no rotation of the refresh token or revocation of the old token. If a refresh token is compromised, an attacker can continue to obtain new access tokens until expiry without detection, potentially bypassing per-token revocation via session_active alone.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Implement refresh token rotation: issue a new refresh token on every refresh, store a token identifier (jti) per token in the DB, and revoke previous tokens for that user. Validate jti on each request and reject reused tokens. Consider maintaining a token revocation list or a per-user token store.
vulnerabilities.snippet: return {"access_token": create_access_token(user.email), "refresh_token": create_refresh_token(user.email)}  # rotate refresh token should also be issued here and old token revoked

vulnerabilities.title: Unsafe parsing of Authorization header in get_user route
vulnerabilities.description: The code directly splits the Authorization header by space and grabs index [1]. If the header is missing, malformed, or does not contain a Bearer token, this raises an exception (IndexError) leading to 500 errors or unintended behavior. This can be exploited to cause errors or bypass authentication in edge cases.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Validate the header format before parsing. Use a dedicated dependency (e.g., OAuth2PasswordBearer) to extract the token securely, or implement robust parsing: if not Authorization or not Authorization.startswith('Bearer '): raise HTTPException(401,...).
vulnerabilities.snippet: access_token = Authorization.split(" ")[1]  # vulnerable if header missing or malformed\n# should instead validate format and extract token safely
